lead: A 3D position tracker reports the pose of a sensor: its position in three axes and its orientation, in a fixed reference frame, many times a second. VR and AR need this because the picture must follow the head, hand or tool. Each tracker family measures a different physical quantity, so each trades workspace, accuracy, latency and immunity to interference differently. Trackers drive head-mounted displays, motion capture, surgical navigation and phone AR.
prereq: You need Chapter 2.1 for degrees of freedom, resolution, accuracy and latency, and Unit 4 for the transforms that turn tracker readings into poses.

blocks.text: A tracker gives a pose, written (x, y, z, yaw, pitch, roll). x, y and z are metres from a fixed origin. Yaw, pitch and roll are rotations about vertical, left-right and forward axes, in degrees. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) tracker reports all six; a 3-DOF tracker reports orientation only. The frame is the fixed coordinate system the host software uses.

Update rate is reports per second, in hertz. Latency is the delay from motion to a new report, in milliseconds. Workspace is the volume where readings stay valid, in cubic metres. Accuracy is closeness to truth; resolution is the smallest change it can show. A fine resolution with a large systematic offset is still inaccurate. A tethered tracker has a cable to the host; a wireless one does not.
Trackers exist because no single sensor gives fast, accurate, untethered pose in every room. The designer picks the family that matches the workspace and the disturbance.

A mechanical tracker is a linked arm. Joints hold encoders that measure angle. Forward kinematics multiplies link transforms to give the tip pose. Workspace is the arm's reach, typically a cubic metre or two. Accuracy is high, often under a millimetre, and latency is low. It is tethered and contact-based, so it suits a tool or a hand, not a walking user.

A magnetic tracker drives three coils in a transmitter and senses the induced signal in a receiver. AC and DC forms differ in pulse timing. It gives 6-DOF through a non-metal body, with no line of sight. Workspace is a few metres around the transmitter. Accuracy is millimetres to a centimetre. Steel, rebar and CRT monitors distort the field, so readings bend near metal.

An ultrasonic tracker times a pulse from an emitter to a microphone. Distance is d = v × t, where v is the speed of sound in air (about 343 m/s at 20 °C) and t is time of flight in seconds. Three or more distances give position by triangulation. Workspace is a room. Accuracy is millimetres. Air temperature and echoes disturb it; it needs line of sight.

An optical tracker uses cameras to see markers or LEDs. Outside-in systems put cameras in the room and markers on the user; inside-out systems put cameras on the headset and markers in the room. It gives 6-DOF with millimetre accuracy over a room. It needs line of sight and is disturbed by bright sunlight or occlusion. Latency is a few milliseconds.

An inertial tracker measures angular rate with a gyroscope and linear acceleration plus gravity with an accelerometer. Integrating rate gives angle, but small bias accumulates as drift. It is wireless, fast and never occluded. It cannot give absolute position alone.

A hybrid tracker fuses optical and inertial data. Optical fixes drift; inertial fills gaps between camera frames. Almost every modern headset uses this pair. Choose mechanical for a fixed tool, magnetic for a body inside a metal-free volume, ultrasonic for a cheap room, optical for a room-scale headset, inertial for fast rotation, and hybrid for both.

spec.aria: Two arrows from an emitter to a microphone for the same 2.9 millisecond echo: 0.995 m at 20 degrees and 1.012 m at 30 degrees, with the 17.4 mm difference marked.

examples.question: An ultrasonic tracker measures a time of flight of 2.9 ms from an emitter to a microphone. The speed of sound in air at 20 °C is 343 m/s. (a) Find the distance. (b) Three such distances from fixed emitters give position; if each distance has 1 mm error, state the order of position error. (c) At 30 °C the speed is 349 m/s. What distance does the same 2.9 ms report?
steps: (b) Each distance error is 1 mm = 0.001 m; geometry maps it almost directly, so position error is about 1 mm.
Change = 1.0121 − 0.9947 = 0.0174 m = 17.4 mm longer with no motion.
examples.answer: (a) 0.995 m; (b) about 1 mm; (c) 1.012 m, about 17.4 mm longer than at 20 °C.
examples.check:
v20 = 343
v30 = 349
t = 0.0029
d20 = v20 * t
d30 = v30 * t
print(round(d20, 3))
print(round(d30, 3))
print(round((d30 - d20) * 1000, 1))
print(0.001)

traps: Resolution is not accuracy: a 0.1 mm resolution with a 5 mm bias is inaccurate.
An ultrasonic distance depends on the speed of sound; a warm room looks like a moved sensor.
Magnetic trackers fail near steel and CRT monitors; the error is not random noise.
Inertial tracking drifts: integrating gyro rate accumulates bias, so it needs an absolute fix.

quiz.q: Name the two quantities in a 6-DOF pose.
quiz.a: Position (x, y, z) and orientation (yaw, pitch, roll).

quiz.q: Why does an inertial tracker drift?
quiz.a: A gyroscope measures rate, not angle. Integrating the rate accumulates small bias and noise, so the angle slowly moves away from truth.

quiz.q: A pulse takes 1.5 ms; v = 343 m/s. Find the distance.
A magnetic tracker reading jumps near a steel desk. Explain.
quiz.a: Steel distorts the transmitted field. The receiver senses a changed field and reports a wrong pose. The jump is systematic distortion, not random noise.

quiz.q: Which tracker family uses time of flight?
Why is optical tracking called outside-in or inside-out?
quiz.a: Outside-in puts cameras in the room looking at the user. Inside-out puts cameras on the user or headset looking at the room.

quiz.q: At 30 °C v = 349 m/s, t = 2.0 ms. Find the distance.

beyond: Not for the exam. Phone AR uses inside-out optical tracking plus inertial sensors, and the fusion runs on a low-power chip. Research pushes toward markerless body tracking and shared multi-camera rooms. Search terms: visual-inertial odometry, magnetic distortion mapping, ultrasonic trilateration, tracker latency budget.
